finding: The no-v1-name text rule misses `afk` followed by a backslash, a quote, a bracket or end of line. The lookahead allows only `[-_:./a-z0-9]`, so a Windows data-folder path, a quoted storage key and a CSS class pass the check.
why: PRD AC-019 / SDD §8 'no-v1-name rule' require the plugin check to fail on a v1 name in the data folder, storage keys and CSS classes. A ported v1 module that still writes %LOCALAPPDATA%\afk\... or uses the key 'afk' passes the gate that the 'renamed in one pass' rule relies on.
fix: Flag `afk` not followed by `v2` at a word boundary on both sides, e.g. `(?<![a-z0-9])afk(?!v2)(?![a-z])` (case-insensitive), and let the URL scrub plus the allow-list handle prose; add test cases for `\afk\`, `"afk"`, `'afk'` and `class="afk"`.
evidence: `re.compile(r"(?<![a-z0-9])afk(?!v2)(?=[-_:./a-z0-9])", re.IGNORECASE)`. Probe against V1_TEXT: `set D=%LOCALAPPDATA%\afk\state` -> False, `Path("afk")` -> False, `localStorage.getItem('afk')` -> False, `class="afk"` -> False, `C:\afk` -> False (each should be True).

finding: Parallel hook runs race on one fired-record file. The last line truncates %LOCALAPPDATA%\afkv2\fired-claude.txt; when two subagents (or a subagent and the session) start at the same time, cmd's redirect hits a sharing violation and the hook exits 1. session-start.cmd:7 writes the same file and has the same defect.
why: The hook's exit code is the redirect's errorlevel. A non-zero exit is a non-blocking hook error; Claude processes hook JSON only on exit 0 (likely, per Claude hooks docs; not re-verified here), so the subagent gets no hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext and runs without the core behaviors. Parallel subagent fan-out in one message is a normal path.
fix: Make the fired-record write unable to fail the hook: `> "%AFKV2_DATA%\fired-%~1.txt" echo ... 2>nul` followed by `exit /b 0` (the text was already printed). Add a test that starts N hooks at once and asserts every exit code is 0.
evidence: `> "%AFKV2_DATA%\fired-%~1.txt" echo %~1 subagent-start %DATE% %TIME%`. Probe (scratch LOCALAPPDATA, 24 concurrent `cmd /d /c subagent-start.cmd claude`, 10 rounds x 3): exit=1 in 18/240, 1/240, 6/240 runs, stderr 'The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.'

finding: With LOCALAPPDATA unset the hooks write the fired record to `\afkv2` at the current drive root, while the config reader refuses the same case
why: The frozen data folder is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\afkv2` (SDD §8); an empty variable expands to `\afkv2`, so the fired record lands outside the data folder that S3 setup reads (no record found, proof fails) and the two components disagree; whether any harness strips LOCALAPPDATA from the hook environment is not verified, and every test sets it.
fix: In both .cmd hooks, skip the record write (exit 0 after printing) when LOCALAPPDATA is not defined, and add a hook test that runs without LOCALAPPDATA and asserts no file outside the data folder.
evidence: set "AFKV2_DATA=%LOCALAPPDATA%\afkv2"  (also subagent-start.cmd:8)  vs afkv2_config.py:55 raise Refusal("no-data-folder", "LOCALAPPDATA is not set; the afkv2 data folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\\afkv2")

finding: The Codex manifest has no install path. Codex reads this repository's marketplace from .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, which still lists only the v1 'afk' entry. The slice added afkv2 only to the Claude marketplace (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json). So the owner-run Codex live check, step 3 ('Enable afkv2 in Codex from the plugin marketplace of this repository'), cannot be done as written, and the Codex hook is never loaded.
why: The Codex manifest has no consumer: nothing installs it. The 0001 Scope did not list .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, and no plan file under docs/afk/afkv2 names it (search: rg 'agents/plugins' docs/afk/afkv2 finds only an investigation ledger). The PRD AC-011/AC-012 Codex proofs depend on this install path.
fix: Add an afkv2 entry (source path ./afkv2) to .agents/plugins/marketplace.json and leave the v1 entry byte-identical, through a scope amendment to 0001 or a new subtask. Or record an IOU that names the subtask that will add it. Then update CODEX-LIVE-CHECKS.md step 3 to name the marketplace entry.
evidence: PROVIDERS.md 'Distribution law': '`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is committed, because `codex plugin marketplace add` reads the Codex marketplace manifest from that path.'; .agents/plugins/marketplace.json plugins = [{"name": "afk", ...}] only; CODEX-LIVE-CHECKS.md:11 '3. Enable afkv2 in Codex from the plugin marketplace of this repository.'

finding: The 'parses no shell command' half of AC-013 is proved only by a deny-list grep of the .cmd source. The payload carries a destructive command (`git status && del /q *`), but no test observes whether it runs. run_hook sets no cwd, so the hook inherits the pytest cwd (probably the worktree).
why: A deny-list misses readers it does not name (for example `type con`, `copy con`, `<` redirection into a sub-shell). If a future hook does run the payload, the observable result is files deleted from the caller's folder, not a failing assert. The test has no behavioural oracle for the property it claims.
fix: Set cwd=tmp_path in run_hook and use a harmless, observable canary in the payload (for example a command that creates tmp_path/canary.txt). Assert the canary does not exist after each hook run. Keep the deny-list as a secondary check.

finding: test_rule_text_reaches_a_session_only_through_the_plugin stands in for AC-011 ('with afkv2 disabled, a new session holds no afkv2 rule text'). It checks only for the marker string, and only in this repo's root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, behind `if path.is_file()`. Rule text copied without the marker line passes. A missing file passes without a check.
why: The proxy checks a different property (no marker token in 2 files) from the acceptance property (no rule body in a session that has the plugin disabled). The conditional means the assert can run zero times and the test stays green.
fix: Assert on the rule body. For each non-trivial line of core/CORE-BEHAVIORS.md, assert it is absent from every instruction file the test checks. Split the conditional: assert that the expected instruction files exist, or parameterize over existing paths so that a skip shows as a skip. Label the test as a static proxy, because the live disabled-session check is the real proof.

criterion: Walk every ## Acceptance bullet (live check on Claude: non-interactive session reports the end marker with the right sha12, also after a compaction, PRD AC-012)
finding: Live-check record proves the post-compaction case by transcript content, not by the session reporting the end marker, and does not say the session was non-interactive
why: The bullet asks that the session reports the end marker with the right sha12 after a compaction; the journal shows a quote only before /compact and a transcript inspection after it.
fix: Add to the live-check record that the session quoted the end marker with 7f976c7ee15c after /compact (and the session mode used), or state why the transcript evidence is accepted instead.
evidence: a new session quoted "afkv2-core-behaviors end 7f976c7ee15c" (matches the build), the transcript holds the hook text again after /compact (SessionStart:compact)

criterion: Confirm every changed path matches a ## Scope glob (out-of-scope file = finding)
finding: Three changed files match no 0001 ## Scope glob: afkv2/core/CORE-BEHAVIORS.md, afkv2/hooks/built/afkv2-core-behaviors.txt, afkv2/hooks/built/afkv2-core-behaviors.claude-subagent.json. Contract 0002 ## Scope owns them ('afkv2/core/CORE-BEHAVIORS.md', 'afkv2/hooks/built/*').
why: The slice writes into another subtask's lane. The executor disclosed it (DECISIONS.md D-1, option A: placeholder source + generated files, needed so 0001's static tier 'plugin_check.py exit 0 on the tree' and the live end-marker check can pass), so the risk is low: 0002 replaces the text and rebuilds. The real defect is the 0001 contract: its own Verification needs paths its Scope omits.
fix: Keep D-1 as recorded, and amend the 0001 ## Scope to list the placeholder source and afkv2/hooks/built/* as 'seed only; 0002 owns the content', or let the human accept the D-1 overlap explicitly. Make sure 0002 knows it edits existing files, not new ones.
evidence: 0001 ## Scope lists no afkv2/core or afkv2/hooks/built path; diff: '+Placeholder text. Subtask 0002 writes the rules.'; DECISIONS.md D-1: 'Supersedes: none (0001 `## Scope` does not list the two paths; 0002 `## Scope` keeps them)'

finding: The prefix/substring marker cases use only inline literals. No case checks a marker held in a constant and matched on another line. The shipped suite holds that pattern itself (test_hooks.py line 150: `assert marker not in path.read_text(...)` with `marker = plugin_check.MARKER`), and check_marker_matching passes it. DECISIONS D-4 records this as a known gap, but no test pins the gap.
why: The acceptance bullet reads as 'fails on code that matches a marker by a prefix or substring'. The suite does not show the main real-world form (a named constant with `in`/startswith) and is silent on it, so a reader can think the gap is closed.
fix: Add the constant-indirection case as an xfail(strict=True) with reason='D-4 known gap: same-line rule only'. The gap then stays visible, and a future data-flow fix turns it green.

finding: The 'C:/abs' refusal case depends on the platform. On POSIX, PurePath('C:/abs').anchor is '' (I checked PurePosixPath), so the reader accepts the value and this case fails. test_config.py has no Windows skip, but test_hooks.py does. No POSIX absolute case ('/abs') exists either.
why: The test assumes the platform without saying so. The repo CI matrix runs ubuntu-latest, so the suite fails there if afkv2/tests is ever added to CI (today tests.yml runs only scripts/tests).
fix: Mark the drive-letter case with skipif(sys.platform != 'win32'), or test PureWindowsPath semantics explicitly. Add a '/abs' case that holds on both platforms.

finding: The 50 ms median check measures wall-clock time around subprocess.run in the unit suite. That time includes Python process creation and cmd.exe startup, and there is no warm-up run. On a loaded Windows host the median can exceed 50 ms while the hook itself does not change.
why: This is a wall-clock assertion in the unit tier. A pass is valid evidence because the measurement overestimates, but a fail is not proof of a slow hook, so the test can fail intermittently.
fix: Add 1 discarded warm-up run before the 7 timed runs. Keep the timing test in the integration tier only, as the contract table places it, for example behind a marker that the unit command deselects.

finding: No test runs a hook with the prebuilt file missing. The `type ... || exit /b 1` branch in both .cmd hooks makes sure that no fired record is written when no text was printed. The setup proof depends on that relation (fired record => text printed), and no test checks it.
why: This is the negative branch of the fired-record behaviour. A regression that writes the record before or despite a failed `type` would make the setup proof falsely green.
fix: Copy the hooks folder into tmp_path without built/, run each hook, and assert a non-zero exit, empty stdout, and no fired-<provider>.txt.

finding: The marketplace test checks only the v1 entry's `source` field. The acceptance bullet requires that the v1 entry stays byte-identical. Today the diff leaves it unchanged (checked with git diff), but the test would pass if a later change edited the v1 name/description/version. Also, test_manifests_must_name_the_plugin_afkv2 changes only the Claude manifest. The Codex manifest name check has no negative case.
why: The asserts are weaker than the property they stand in for.
fix: Compare the v1 entry to a pinned expected dict (or to the base-branch blob via git show). Parameterize the manifest-name negative test over plugin_check.MANIFESTS.

finding: The stale check is blind to line endings. `read_text` uses universal newlines, so a prebuilt file converted to CRLF compares equal and passes, while the hook `type`s the CRLF bytes.
why: The repository runs core.autocrlf=true (.gitattributes header) and no attribute pins afkv2/hooks/built/* to LF, so a fresh clone or a harness plugin-cache copy can hold CRLF built files; the printed text then differs byte-for-byte from the build output and the marker lines end in \r, which a full-line compare on the reader side can reject.
evidence: `elif path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != text:`. Probe on a scratch copy of afkv2/: rewrite hooks/built/afkv2-core-behaviors.txt with CRLF -> run_checks() returns [] (no 'stale').

finding: A hooks.json whose `hooks` value is null (or not an object) crashes the check with a traceback instead of a problem line and the JSON answer.
why: `hooks.get("hooks", {})` returns None for an explicit null, and `event not in None` raises TypeError; a string value would do a substring test instead of a key test.
fix: `events = hooks.get("hooks"); if not isinstance(events, dict): problems.append(f"{HOOKS_FILE.as_posix()}: hooks must be an object")` before the event loop.
evidence: `events = hooks.get("hooks", {})`. Probe: scratch tree with hooks/hooks.json = `{"hooks": null}` -> run_checks() raises TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not a container or iterable.

finding: `-h`/`--help` bypasses the JSON envelope: argparse prints plain usage text and exits 0, so a caller parsing stdout as one JSON object fails on an exit code that says ok.
why: The module contract (docstring line 3, SDD §8 'one read command, JSON answer') is one JSON object on every exit; `_Parser.error` covers bad arguments but not the help action.
fix: `_Parser(prog=..., add_help=False)` so `-h` becomes a usage refusal (exit 2, JSON).
evidence: `parser = _Parser(prog="afkv2_config.py")`. Probe: `python -I afkv2_config.py --help` -> plain 'usage: afkv2_config.py [-h] ...' text, exit=0.

finding: Which bytes does 'the text between the marker lines' mean? The build hashes the body without its final newline, but the bytes between the end of the begin line and the start of the end line are body + "\n".
why: SDD §8 'marker hash' is frozen on day 1 and S3 setup proof recomputes it; a consumer that takes the literal byte span gets a different sha12 than the build. Pinning the definition now (in the SDD row or a docstring the consumer can cite) avoids a false 'hook did not fire' later.
fix: State the definition in one home: 'lines between the marker lines, joined with \n, no trailing newline' (current behavior), and point S3 at `marker_hash`.
evidence:
`body = source_text.replace("
", "
").rstrip("
"); sha = marker_hash(body)`; plain = `begin sha
` + body + `
end sha
`. Input: body 'x' -> hashed bytes 'x', literal span between marker lines 'x
'.
